title: Nayaks of Thanjavur
capsule: The Thanjavur Nayak kingdom was established around 1532 when the Vijayanagara emperor appointed Sevappa Nayak as governor of the Thanjavur region in the Kaveri delta of Tamil Nadu, and the governorship quickly became hereditary and effectively sovereign. The dynasty reached its cultural apex under Raghunatha Nayak (r. 1600–1634), a composer and polymath who patronized Telugu and Tamil literature and presided over a court that attracted scholars from across South India. Vijaya Raghava Nayak, the last ruler, was killed in 1673 when the Madurai Nayak Chokkanatha invaded; the Marathas under Venkoji (Ekoji I) subsequently captured Thanjavur in 1674, ending the Nayak line.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Thanjavur Nayak kingdom's core territory around the Kaveri delta is well defined by Vijayanagara and later Maratha records; the extent of nominal suzerainty in the surrounding districts is less precisely mapped.
